Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Alex / Sofia  thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our call so we have a single source of truth.

Key pain points you described:
- User-facing search assistant currently facing tail latency spikes during peak hours (holiday traffic).
- Cost per inference is high for the 3B model at current traffic and concurrency.
- Need deterministic latency for query routing and SLAs with partners.

Goals we discussed:
- Target p95 latency <= 200ms for 512-token generation on user flows.
- Support sustained 150 QPS with 2.5x headroom for bursts (target peak 375 QPS).
- Keep per-token inference cost within your current budget threshold (TBD exact $/k token).

Agreed technical follow-ups (action items):
1) I will send a detailed SLO/throughput breakdown and recommended deployment topology (attached).
2) You will share current peak QPS, average request size (tokens), and any expected seasonal multipliers.
3) Schedule follow-up for capacity sizing and Dedicated quote (David / Michael will join).

Attachments: acme-slo-table.xlsx, redwood-deployment-diagram.png

Next steps:
- Marissa to propose a configuration for Dedicated capacity and a fallback hosted routing plan by EOD 6/2.
- Alex to share traffic profile and any internal SLA thresholds.

Thanks  I captured the items in the attached SLO table.


Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa  appreciate the recap and attachments. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Current baseline: 120 QPS sustained, average request = 420 tokens (prompt+response), typical response length ~180 tokens.
- Peak multiplier: historically we see up to 3x during launches/promotions (~360 QPS sustained for short windows).
- Current p95 for the existing setup is ~480ms and spikes to >900ms under peak.

Questions for your sizing:
1) Can you confirm what p95 numbers you expect for the two model variants we discussed (redwood-3-small and redwood-3-large) at 420 tokens?
2) What batching strategy / batch size do you recommend for low-latency user flows vs. background inference?

We'll also need an outline of how Dedicated capacity + hosted fallback would work across regions (we have primary users in US, EU).

Sofia and I are available for a follow-up on Wednesday 6/2 afternoon PT.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@acme.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T13:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Alex / Sofia  great context, thanks. Below is a technical deep-dive recap with explicit SLO estimates, model recommendations, and a proposed deployment topology. See attached spreadsheet and diagram for the numeric tables and topology image.

Executive SLO recommendations (targets we can reasonably hit with Dedicated + optimizations):
- Redwood-3-small (quantized int8): p50 ~ 40-60ms, p95 ~ 140-220ms at 512 tokens; for 420 tokens expect ~p95 120-180ms.
- Redwood-3-large (int8/float16): p50 ~ 80-120ms, p95 ~ 240-350ms at 512 tokens; for 420 tokens expect ~p95 200-300ms.

Throughput and capacity guidance:
- Baseline sustained 150 QPS: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs in Dedicated with continuous batching and KV cache for session-based flows (gives headroom and efficient batching).
- Peak 375 QPS (3x): recommend 5 x A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale policy to add capacity at 200 QPS increments or use burst capacity on hosted pool.
- Efficiency knobs: 8-16 token batching for user-facing flows, dynamic batching cutoff at 120ms to avoid perceptible latency; background batch jobs can use larger batch sizes (32-64).

Latency strategies and trade-offs:
- Use prefix/KV caching for multi-turn flows to reduce compute per-request by ~30-60% depending on context length.
- For strict p95 SLAs, prefer Dedicated lanes with reserved GPUs and per-tenant isolation; fallback to hosted variants in a different region if Dedicated capacity is saturated.
- Quantization: int8 gives 1.8-2.5x throughput improvement with modest quality delta; recommend testing redwood-3-small int8 for user flows.

Deployment topology (high level):
- Primary: Dedicated cluster in us-west with 3 nodes (2 reserved for sustained, 1 autoscale/burst).
- Secondary: Hosted fallback in us-east + EU-region routing via smart routing policy (failover + gradual reroute).
- Networking: VPC peering or PrivateLink for secure traffic; TLS + mTLS between Acme services and Redwood ingress.

Attachments referenced: acme-slo-table.xlsx (SLO numbers and per-model perf), redwood-deployment-diagram.png (topology). Also linking a sample Dedicated quote for similar profiles.

Open items / asks for sizing:
- Confirm acceptable p95 target for user-facing flows (is 200ms target firm?).
- Share token distribution percentiles (p50/p90/p95) if available.
- Indicate whether session affinity is required for KV cache benefits (multi-turn chat).

Next steps we propose:
1) We prepare a Dedicated capacity proposal & cost estimate (David will lead) and a fallback hosted routing config (Michael).
2) Joint call Wed 6/2 2:30pm PT to align on final SLOs and traffic numbers.

If this looks right, I'll kick off the quote and share a first-pass cost/throughput table by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks  attaching the files again.


Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
